description: Recover the canonical MCP tool discovery, validation, run, status, and result loopback for dynamic workflows by exposing Factory Session-oriented tools backed by deterministic mock session-provider fixtures, with focused tests proving discovery and invocation without host packaging.

context.customerAsk: Recover canonical MCP tool discovery, validation, run, status, and result behavior so an MCP client can discover Factory Session-oriented tools, validate a JavaScript workflow fixture, start a mock-backed session, poll status, and read final or partial results.
context.problem: The earlier dynamic-workflows-cell-mcp-tools work is blocked by failed paired plan-token recovery, and downstream MCP install or real-runtime swap-in work has no narrow, verified canonical tool contract to depend on.
context.solution: Define or repair canonical Factory Session MCP tools for list, validate, run simple, run async, status, result, dispatches, artifacts, controls, and events; keep workflow-named tools as compatibility aliases; wire behavior to deterministic mock session-provider fixtures or shared session execution interfaces; and add focused MCP registry or mock-client tests for discovery and invocation.

acceptanceCriteria: MCP tool discovery exposes canonical Factory Session-oriented tools with stable request and response schemas for list, validate, run simple, run async, status, result, dispatches, artifacts, controls, and events.
Workflow-named MCP aliases remain compatibility-only and invoke the same Factory Session implementations and response shapes as the canonical tools.
MCP validate and run simple tools return deterministic fixture success responses and typed validation failure responses.
MCP run async, status, and result tools cover completed, running/not-ready, failed-with-partial-result, missing-session, and request-conflict cases with deterministic typed responses.
Tool implementation uses deterministic mock session-provider fixtures or shared session execution interfaces and does not add dependencies on API handlers or host packaging.
Focused MCP registry or mock-client tests prove tool discovery and invocation without requiring Cursor, OpenCode, Codex, Kiro, Gemini, Claude Code, or other host packaging.
Typecheck, lint, and targeted tests including go test ./pkg/mcp/... ./pkg/factorysessionexecution pass.

userStories.title: Discover canonical Factory Session MCP tools
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I want to discover stable Factory Session-oriented tool names and schemas so I can integrate with dynamic workflow sessions without relying on transitional workflow terminology.
acceptanceCriteria: MCP discovery includes canonical Factory Session tools for session list, validate, run simple, run async, status, result, dispatches, artifacts, controls, and events.

Each canonical tool exposes a deterministic input schema and response schema with Factory Session vocabulary such as session_id, status, diagnostics, dispatches, artifacts, events, and typed errors where applicable.
Workflow-named tool aliases, if present, are marked or documented as compatibility-only and resolve to the same behavior and response shape as their canonical Factory Session tool.

A focused MCP registry or mock-client test asserts discovery of the canonical tools and verifies one compatibility alias maps to the same implementation behavior without asserting unrelated package or route inventories.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Validate JavaScript workflow fixtures through MCP
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I want validation to return deterministic success and typed failure responses so I can check workflow source before starting a Factory Session.
acceptanceCriteria: Invoking the canonical validate tool with the simple valid JavaScript workflow fixture returns a deterministic success response that includes validation status and any expected normalized metadata.

Invoking the canonical validate tool with an invalid fixture returns a typed validation failure response with stable diagnostic fields and no unstructured panic or transport-level failure for expected validation errors.
Workflow-named validate alias invocation returns the same success and typed validation failure semantics as the canonical validate tool.
Validation invocation uses deterministic fixtures or shared session execution interfaces and does not depend on API handlers or external provider credentials.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Run a simple mock-backed Factory Session through MCP
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I want to start a simple mock-backed Factory Session and read its completed result so I can prove the MCP loopback works before real runtime swap-in.
acceptanceCriteria: Invoking the canonical run simple tool with the deterministic simple workflow fixture returns a success response containing a stable Factory Session identifier, completed status, and final result payload or result reference.
The result tool can read the same completed session and returns the expected deterministic final result without requiring a separate host installation step.
Repeating the same deterministic fixture invocation produces stable reviewer-verifiable values for session identity policy, status, and result content where the fixture contract defines stability.
The run simple path uses the mock session-provider fixture or shared session execution interface and avoids direct API-handler dependencies.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Support async status and not-ready result polling
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I want async run, status, and result tools to represent running and not-ready states consistently so host agents can poll without treating in-progress work as a failure.
acceptanceCriteria: Invoking the canonical run async tool with a running fixture returns a Factory Session identifier and an in-progress status rather than a completed final result.
The status tool returns a deterministic running or not-ready response for the in-progress mock session.
The result tool returns a typed not-ready response for the in-progress session without losing the session identifier or returning an untyped error.
A later completed fixture state for the same session can be observed through status and result with completed status and the expected final result.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Return typed responses for failure, missing session, and conflict cases
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I want predictable status and result errors for failed, missing, and conflicting requests so agent hosts can recover or report the right failure reason.
acceptanceCriteria: Status and result tools return deterministic typed responses for a failed session that includes a partial result or partial artifact reference when the fixture defines one.
Status and result tools return a typed missing-session response for an unknown Factory Session identifier.
Run or result requests that conflict with an existing request/session fixture return a typed request-conflict response with stable machine-readable fields.
Failure-path tests assert observable MCP response semantics and do not require scanning source-file structure, command inventories, or host package configuration.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Inspect dispatches, artifacts, controls, and events through MCP fixtures
userStories.description: As an MCP client, I want inspection and control tools to expose deterministic session-owned dispatches, artifacts, controls, and events so host agents can inspect mock-backed Factory Sessions through the same vocabulary later used by the real runtime.
acceptanceCriteria: Dispatch inspection returns deterministic session-owned dispatch records for the mock fixture using Factory Session and Dispatch vocabulary.
Artifact inspection returns deterministic session-owned artifact records or content references for the mock fixture using FactoryArtifact vocabulary.
Event inspection returns ordered Factory Session event facts for the mock fixture without exposing internal Petri-net terminology as the primary public vocabulary.
Control tool invocation returns deterministic accepted, rejected, or unsupported responses for the fixture-defined control cases without mutating unrelated sessions.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
